title: Conformance matrix, Phase 7 (NRF: Nnrf_NFManagement, Nnrf_NFDiscovery, Nnrf_AccessToken; discovery in the other functions; AUSF: Nausf_UEAuthentication, Nausf_SoRProtection, Nausf_UPUProtection; UDR: Nudr_DataRepository, Nudr_GroupIDmap; NSSF: Nnssf_NSSelection, Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability; NEF: TrafficInfluence, MonitoringEvent, AsSessionWithQoS; SCP: indirect communication; BSF: Nbsf_Management; PCF: Npcf_PolicyAuthorization)
note: Same rules as the other matrices. 'verified' = tests pass and an independent peer (Open5GS's functions and its NRF as the reference, UERANSIM end to end) confirms it. The gap rows are what the phase leaves out so far.

rows.procedure: NFRegister: PUT of the NFProfile; 201 with Location, ETag and the heart-beat timer; refusals (400) for a malformed profile, an id that differs from the URI, a missing nfType, a bad nfStatus, bad lists; custom NF types and vendor attributes are stored; the registry fills priority / capacity / load / plmnList when absent
rows.evidence: Open5GS's AUSF, UDR, UDM, BSF, PCF, NSSF, SMF and AMF register at our NRF in oracle scenario S3 (OUR_NRF=1) and complete the registration, session and release; the differential against Open5GS's NRF gives the same status codes.

rows.procedure: NFUpdate by replacement (PUT on an existing instance: 200) and by JSON Patch (PATCH: 200 with the profile; 404, 409 for a non-existing attribute, 412 for a stale If-Match, 400 for an immutable attribute, a bad status or a malformed patch)
rows.evidence: End-to-end with the HTTP/2 client; the patch engine is the shared RFC 6902 implementation.

rows.procedure: NF heart-beat: PATCH replace /nfStatus (and /load): 204 and no new entity tag when nothing changed; a function back from SUSPENDED gets 200 with its profile; UNDISCOVERABLE accepted
rows.evidence: Open5GS's functions and ours heart-beat at our NRF for the length of the oracle scenarios.

rows.procedure: heart-beat supervision: a function that misses suspend_after heart-beats becomes SUSPENDED (not discoverable, subscribers notified); after purge_after seconds the profile is removed and NF_DEREGISTERED is sent
rows.evidence: Timers shortened in the test (1 s heart-beat, 2 missed, 3 s purge).

rows.procedure: NFDeregister: DELETE; 204, 404 when unknown; subscribers get NF_DEREGISTERED
rows.evidence: Every oracle scenario ends with the functions deregistering from our NRF.

rows.procedure: NFListRetrieval (nf-type, limit; UriList with _links.item) and NFProfileRetrieval (200, 404; the services as the nfServices array, or the nfServiceList map for a consumer that indicates the Service-Map feature)
rows.evidence: Differential: the reference answers a retrieval with the map unasked, ours follows NOTE 15 (array unless Service-Map is indicated).

rows.procedure: NFStatusSubscribe / Update / Unsubscribe: nfStatusNotificationUri, subscrCond (nfInstanceId, nfType, serviceName, amfSetId / amfRegionId, snssaiList, nfGroupId), reqNotifEvents, notifCondition (monitored / unmonitored attributes), validityTime; 201 with Location and subscriptionId; validity extension by PATCH; 404, 400 for unsupported conditions
rows.evidence: Open5GS's functions subscribe at our NRF and receive the status notifications in the oracle scenarios.

rows.procedure: NFStatusNotify: POST NotificationData (NF_REGISTERED, NF_PROFILE_CHANGED, NF_DEREGISTERED) with nfInstanceUri and the profile in the subscriber's representation of the services; a load report alone is not a change; three attempts
rows.evidence: A callback server in the test receives and decodes each notification.

rows.procedure: OPTIONS on nf-instances answers with the capabilities

NFDiscover: target-nf-type and requester-nf-type mandatory; only REGISTERED instances; service-names (comma separated list, or repeated) with the services of the answer reduced to the intersection; snssais and target-plmn-list as JSON arrays; dnn, tai, guami, amf-set-id, amf-region-id, supi (ranges and patterns), target-nf-instance-id; allowedNfTypes of the profile and of its services; limit; unknown parameters ignored; complexQuery refused
rows.evidence: Our AMF, SMF, UDM, PCF and AUSF find their peers through it in the cluster and in the oracle (S3-S5); Open5GS's AMF, SMF and AUSF find ours. The differential has the same status codes for every query including the refusals.

rows.procedure: result order: preferred-locality first, then priority (lower first), then load; validityPeriod and nrfSupportedFeatures in the answer
Service-Map feature (supported-features): nfServiceList map or nfServices array in discovery, retrieval and notifications
rows.evidence: Found by the oracle run: Open5GS's functions register with the map and its clients expect the array; the first version of the NRF returned the map and the AMF could not reach the AUSF.

rows.procedure: discovery client shared by the functions: apiRoot of the first matching instance, cached for the validity period, forgotten after a connection failure
rows.evidence: UDM (UDR), PCF (UDR), AUSF (UDM), SMF (UDM, PCF, AMF) and AMF (AUSF, UDM, PCF, SMF) run with no peer address in their configuration in the cluster tests.

rows.procedure: Access token request: client_credentials grant, form body; the requester must be a registered instance of the stated type; the scope must be offered by a registered producer (or the given instance) that allows the requester's type; 200 with an ES256 JWT (iss, sub, aud, scope, exp), Bearer, expires_in; error body with invalid_request / invalid_client / invalid_scope / unsupported_grant_type
rows.evidence: The test verifies the signature with the public key from /oauth2/jwks and rejects a damaged token, alg none and a malformed one.

rows.procedure: enforcement: with oauth2.enforce the discovery, retrieval, list and subscription endpoints need a bearer token whose audience is the NRF and whose scope covers the service (401, 403); registration, heart-beat and deregistration are authenticated by the transport
the registry survives a restart (state file, written behind); registrations get a full heart-beat interval to come back
rows.evidence: The chaos run kills and restarts the NRF under load; the functions register again by themselves and the recovery wave passes.

rows.procedure: configuration: registry block validated (ranges, unknown keys, enforce needs enabled, the top-level nrf key refused for the NRF itself)
hostile input: replay fuzzing of registration, patch, subscription, discovery query and token request under ASan / UBSan
NRF-to-NRF: registration of an NRF with another, forwarding and redirecting discovery, subscription and token requests, hnrf-uri
rows.evidence: Single NRF per PLMN; the hierarchy comes with the roaming scope, which is out of v1.

rows.procedure: other PLMNs and SNPNs: target-plmn-list towards a home NRF, subscription ids prefixed with the PLMN, SNPN lists
rows.evidence: Roaming is out of scope for v1 (ADR-0003).

rows.procedure: NF sets and groups: nfSetId-based discovery and subscription conditions, nfSetIdList, NF group ids as discovery parameters
rows.evidence: Profiles are stored whole, so a set-aware consumer's attributes are kept; the filters are not implemented.

rows.procedure: ETag / If-Match on PUT (replacement), If-None-Match handling, compression of registration bodies
rows.evidence: Entity tags are issued and honoured for PATCH.

rows.procedure: Authenticate with 5G AKA: POST AuthenticationInfo (SUPI or SUCI, serving network name) gets the vector from the UDM and answers 201 with UEAuthenticationCtx (rand, autn, HXRES*, the 5g-aka link) and Location; the AMF's PUT of RES* is compared with XRES*; 200 with AUTHENTICATION_SUCCESS, SUPI and KSEAF, or AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE without a key; the context is single use
rows.evidence: Open5GS's AMF and UERANSIM register through our AUSF behind Open5GS's UDM and NRF (oracle S3, OUR_AUSF=1), and with every function ours (S3, S4, S5). The differential against Open5GS's AUSF gives the same status codes and attributes for the shared requests; the two documented differences (a second confirmation, the kseaf attribute of a failure) are in tools/ausf_diff.py.

rows.procedure: the serving network name: constructed as 5G:mnc<3>.mcc<3>.3gppnetwork.org, checked by the AUSF before it asks the UDM, restricted to a configured list of serving networks (SERVING_NETWORK_NOT_AUTHORIZED, 403)
synchronisation failure: resynchronizationInfo (RAND, AUTS) is passed to the UDM, a forged AUTS is refused (403), the SQN continues from the UE's
rows.evidence: Open5GS's AMF resynchronises through our AUSF in the oracle scenarios that include a stale SQN.

rows.procedure: a null RES* (no response from the UE, a failed check in the AMF) is a failure; a malformed one is 400; an unknown or expired context is 404 CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND; one pending context per UE and serving network (a new start replaces it); the tables are bounded (503 beyond)

Authenticate with EAP-AKA': the UDM's AV' (RAND, AUTN with the AMF separation bit, XRES, CK', IK') is turned into the EAP-Request/AKA'-Challenge (AT_RAND, AT_AUTN, AT_KDF 1, AT_KDF_INPUT = the serving network name, optional AT_RESULT_IND, AT_MAC) in the 5gAuthData string and the eap-session link; the response is verified (AT_MAC first, then RES; an AT_KDF that asks for another function fails), with a failure notification and EAP-Failure after a failed round, AKA'-Authentication-Reject and Client-Error ending the session, a protected success indication when both sides ask for one, the synchronisation failure answered with a new challenge (at most twice), and EAP-Success with KSEAF (the first 256 bits of the EMSK -> KAUSF -> KSEAF) at the end
rows.evidence: Key derivation: the four test vectors of RFC 9048 Annex D (CK', IK', K_encr, K_aut, K_re, MSK, EMSK) are reproduced. End to end: UERANSIM's own EAP-AKA' peer (nr-ue, with the one-line decoder fix of deploy/oracle/build_ueransim_eap.sh) registers, sets up a PDU session and pings through our NRF, AUSF, AMF, SMF, UPF, UDM and PCF (oracle S3, S5 with AUTH_METHOD=EAP_AKA_PRIME); the AMF carries the challenge in the EAP message of the Authentication request and the EAP-success in the Security mode command (TS 24.501 5.4.1.2.1).

rows.procedure: removal of an authentication result (DELETE on the 5g-aka-confirmation or eap-session resource): 204, the UDM is told (PUT auth-events/{authEventId} with authRemovalInd), only for the current result of the UE; the AMF deletes the result when the UE is de-registered, implicitly de-registered or rejects the security mode command
rows.evidence: In the oracle scenarios our AUSF forwards Open5GS's AMF's DELETE to Open5GS's UDM, which accepts it (it wants success=true next to authRemovalInd: our AUSF sends the specified false first and the other form when the UDM answers 400).

rows.procedure: deregister: POST .../ue-authentications/deregister clears the security context of a SUPI (204; 404 CONTEXT_NOT_FOUND; 400)

FN-RG authentication: POST rg-authentications with the SUCI and the authenticated indication; the UDM's RgAuthCtx gives the SUPI; AUTHENTICATION_SUCCESS with authInd when the W-AGF authenticated the gateway, AUTHENTICATION_FAILURE otherwise
rows.evidence: The UDM side (GET security-information-rg) is part of the same change.

rows.procedure: errors of the UDM mapped as the AUSF table says: USER_NOT_FOUND (404), AUTHENTICATION_REJECTED / SERVING_NETWORK_NOT_AUTHORIZED / INVALID_HN_PUBLIC_KEY_IDENTIFIER / INVALID_SCHEME_OUTPUT (403), UNSUPPORTED_PROTECTION_SCHEME (501), AV_GENERATION_PROBLEM (500), UPSTREAM_SERVER_ERROR and NETWORK_FAILURE (504)

Nausf_SoRProtection generate-sor-data: the SoR header (ACK, list type, list indication), SoR-MAC-IAUSF = the 128 least significant bits of KDF(KAUSF, 0x77, header, CounterSoR, list), SoR-XMAC-IUE = KDF(KAUSF, 0x78, 0x01, CounterSoR); PLMN identities as TS 24.008, access technologies as TS 31.102, secured packets as base64; CounterSoR starts at 1 with every new KAUSF, goes up with every MAC and suspends the service (503 COUNTER_WRAP) at 0xFFFF; 404 without a security context
rows.evidence: The expected MACs in the test are computed from the clauses' own constants and byte strings written out by hand. The consumer side (UDM, AMF, UE) does not exist yet: AUSF-GAP-02.

rows.procedure: Nausf_UPUProtection generate-upu-data: UPU-MAC-IAUSF = KDF(KAUSF, 0x7B, UE parameters update list, CounterUPU) (secured packet, default configured NSSAI and ME routing indicator data sets as TS 24.501 9.11.3.53A encodes them), UPU-XMAC-IUE = KDF(KAUSF, 0x7C, 0x01, CounterUPU); the same counter rules
rows.evidence: As for SoR.

rows.procedure: the latest KAUSF of every authenticated SUPI, with its counters, is kept in an AES-256-GCM wrapped state file (bound to the SUPI) written behind the requests and restored at start-up with the counters ahead of the last values used; a wrong key, a tampered ciphertext, a moved record and a damaged file stop the start
rows.evidence: The chaos run kills and restarts the AUSF under load.

rows.procedure: registration at the NRF with the three services (nausf-auth, nausf-sorprotection, nausf-upuprotection) and ausfInfo (supiRanges, routingIndicators, groupId); the UDM is found through the NRF
rows.evidence: Open5GS's AMF finds our AUSF at Open5GS's NRF and ours; our AMF finds it at ours.

rows.procedure: configuration: the ausf block validated (ranges, unknown keys, serving network names, state file needs the master key, supi_ranges, routing_indicators)
hostile input: replay fuzzing of every request of the three services against a stub UDM with a known EAP-AKA' vector, under ASan / UBSan

every body the AUSF produces (UEAuthenticationCtx for both methods, ConfirmationDataResponse, EapSession in three states, RgAuthCtx, SorSecurityInfo, UpuSecurityInfo, ProblemDetails) validates against the OpenAPI of the pinned specification; so do the UDM's EAP-AKA' vector and RgAuthCtx
rows.evidence: scripts/validate_payloads.ps1: 44 of 44 payloads valid.

rows.procedure: EAP-TLS for N5GC devices and FN-RGs in private networks (n5gcInd, Annex B)
rows.evidence: A request with n5gcInd true is refused (403 AUTHENTICATION_REJECTED).

rows.procedure: the consumers of the protection services: the UDM requesting SoR-MAC-IAUSF / UPU-MAC-IAUSF when it delivers steering information or UE parameters (including the SoR / UPU containers in the AMF's Registration accept and DL NAS transport and the acknowledgement checks), and the UDM clearing a stale context at an old AUSF (deregister)
rows.evidence: The AUSF side is complete and tested through its API; wiring the UDM and the AMF is a Release 15 / 16 feature pass of its own.

rows.procedure: EAP identity exchange (EAP-Request/Identity, AKA'-Identity with AT_*_ID_REQ), pseudonyms and fast re-authentication
rows.evidence: 5GS does not use fast re-authentication (Annex F.3 NOTE 1) and sends the SUCI outside EAP; the AUSF never requests an identity.

rows.procedure: HTTP 307 / 308 redirection (ES3XX) between AUSF instances of a set, indirect communication through an SCP
rows.evidence: One AUSF instance per deployment unit; the SCP is a later function.

rows.procedure: every operation of the four published API files (subscription data, policy data, exposure data, application data: 176 operations, 444 schemas) is generated from the pinned OpenAPI files and served under /nudr-dr/v1 and /nudr-dr/v2, from one engine
rows.evidence: tools/gen_udr_api.py --check proves that the committed tables are those of the pinned files; 19 UDR payloads validate against the OpenAPI.

rows.procedure: Query: GET of a document, of a collection (the children of a path), of a composite parent (ProvisionedDataSets, ContextDataSets); 404 with USER_NOT_FOUND when the subscriber is unknown and DATA_NOT_FOUND when the data is; the SM data filters single-nssai and dnn, the SM policy filters snssai and dnn
rows.evidence: Oracle S3 and S4 with Open5GS's UDM, AUSF, PCF, SMF and AMF against our UDR (OUR_UDR=1): the subscriber is provisioned in Open5GS's document format and UERANSIM registers, opens a PDU session, pings and releases it.

rows.procedure: retrieval of a subset of a resource: ?fields= with JSON pointers (members, members of members, members of every array element); a bare member name is taken as a pointer (Open5GS's UDM sends fields=nssai)
rows.evidence: The differential compares fields=nssai with Open5GS's UDR; Open5GS's UDM's NSSAI query works against our UDR in oracle S3.

rows.procedure: Create: PUT of a new resource answers 201 with the representation and the Location, POST to a collection allocates the identifier and answers 201; a replacing PUT answers 204 (or 200 where the operation lists it); compat.put_no_content answers 204 for Open5GS's UDM
rows.evidence: Oracle S3 and S4 with Open5GS's UDM, AUSF, PCF, SMF and AMF against our UDR (OUR_UDR=1): the subscriber is provisioned in Open5GS's document format and UERANSIM registers, opens a PDU session, pings and releases it.

rows.procedure: Delete: 204; 404 when absent; the subscriber's whole data (DELETE /subscription-data/{ueId}, provisioning extension) removes its aliases too
rows.evidence: Oracle S3 and S4 with Open5GS's UDM, AUSF, PCF, SMF and AMF against our UDR (OUR_UDR=1): the subscriber is provisioned in Open5GS's document format and UERANSIM registers, opens a PDU session, pings and releases it. Open5GS's UDM deletes the SMF registration at release.

rows.procedure: Update: PATCH with JSON Patch (application/json-patch+json, plain application/json taken as one) or merge patch, atomic, the result validated, a failing patch changes nothing (400 MODIFICATION_NOT_ALLOWED); PUT replaces
rows.evidence: Open5GS's UDM updates the SQN with a JSON Patch on the authentication subscription in every registration of oracle S3.

rows.procedure: entity tags and validators: strong ETag (the revision) and Last-Modified on every representation, 304 for If-None-Match and If-Modified-Since, 412 for a failed If-Match / If-None-Match: * on PUT, PATCH and DELETE, checked inside the storage operation (atomic), Cache-Control max-age configurable
rows.evidence: Eight threads create one key: exactly one wins, on every backend.

rows.procedure: bodies are validated against the schemas of the pinned OpenAPI files (type, enum, range, length, pattern, required members, additional properties, combinators) and the document a PATCH produces too; the error names the JSON pointer
rows.evidence: Open5GS's SM data (three allowed SSC modes, schema maximum two) is refused, and the oracle provisions a conforming document: the validator is strict where the reference is not.

rows.procedure: Subscribe and unsubscribe: POST to subs-to-notify of each data set (subscription, policy, exposure, application, influence data), 201 with Location and the subscriptionId, expiry chosen by the UDR (bounded, spread), a bound on the number of subscriptions (429), DELETE to unsubscribe, expired subscriptions removed

Notify on a change of subscription data: DataChangeNotify with NotifyItem / ChangeItem (whole document ADD or REMOVE, else one item per changed member), the originalCallbackReference of a stateless UDM, 3gpp-Sbi-Notification-Correlation suppresses the named subscriptions; delivery by worker threads with retries, a bounded queue and outcome counters
rows.evidence: A real callback server over HTTP/2.

rows.procedure: notifications of policy data (PolicyDataChangeNotification by resource: am-data, sm-data, usage monitoring, operator-specific data, sponsor, BDT, PLMN UE policy; delResources on removal), exposure data (ExposureDataChangeNotification), influence data and application data (TrafficInfluDataNotif, ApplicationDataChangeNotif, filtered by dnns, snssais, internalGroupIds, supis, appIds / dataFilters)
rows.evidence: The notification bodies validate against the OpenAPI schemas of the pinned specification.

rows.procedure: a subscriber addressed by GPSI (msisdn-, extid-) is resolved to its SUPI through the alias index kept from the identity data; S-NSSAI comparison treats the slice differentiator FFFFFF as none
rows.evidence: Open5GS's UDM and SMF send single-nssai {sst, sd: ffffff}; without the equivalence they get no SM data (found by oracle S3).

rows.procedure: the provisioning extension (PUT and DELETE on the GET-only resources, DELETE of a subscriber, listing the subscribers) needs the bearer token, 403 PROVISIONING_DISABLED without one configured; the UDM presents it; the operations of the specification need none
rows.evidence: The cluster runs with a token on the UDR and one on the UDM.

rows.procedure: Nudr_GroupIDmap: GET nf-group-ids with nf-type (list) and subscriberId answers the map NF type -> group id from the configured SUPI ranges; a GPSI is resolved first; 400 for a missing or malformed parameter, 404 when nothing is configured

storage interface (get, put with precondition and replaced record, delete, atomic mutate, prefix listing, partitions) with the same expectations on the memory, the journalled file and the PostgreSQL backend: revisions, preconditions, prefix semantics (keys with LIKE metacharacters and unicode), eight-thread read-modify-write without a lost update
rows.evidence: PostgreSQL 18 started without root for each test run (deploy/run/pg-temp.sh).

rows.procedure: PostgreSQL: one table with jsonb documents, revisions from a sequence, row locks for the transactions, a connection pool, schema version check, an unreachable server is a start-up error; the API tests, the notification tests and the storage tests all run on it

the journalled file store: write-behind journal and snapshot, recovery from a crash image (including a journal older than its snapshot), refusal of an unreadable, corrupt or unwritable store at start-up

registration at the NRF: nudr-dr (v1 and v2 as one service with two versions), nudr-group-id-map and udrInfo (group id, SUPI / GPSI ranges, supported data sets); found by Open5GS's UDM, AUSF and PCF through the NRF
rows.evidence: Oracle S3 and S4 with Open5GS's UDM, AUSF, PCF, SMF and AMF against our UDR (OUR_UDR=1): the subscriber is provisioned in Open5GS's document format and UERANSIM registers, opens a PDU session, pings and releases it.

rows.procedure: configuration: store (memory, file, postgres; the connection string only from the environment or a file), provisioning token (16 characters at least), validation switch, udrInfo ranges, subscription limits, cache, compatibility, group map; unknown keys and bad values refused with the name of the key

hostile input: replay fuzzing of requests to 33 resources with every method, content type, query and precondition, of arbitrary paths and of the group map query, under ASan / UBSan (30,000 mutations per seed run locally)

every body the UDR produces (the composites, registrations, identity data, subscriptions in all five data sets, the five notifications, ProblemDetails for 404 / 400 / 412) validates against the OpenAPI of the pinned specifications
rows.evidence: scripts/validate_payloads.ps1: every payload valid in the run of the time (63 of 63, 19 of them the UDR's; 81 of 81 now).

rows.procedure: Open5GS as the consumer: its UDM, AUSF, PCF, SMF and AMF run their registration, PDU session, policy and release procedures against our UDR
rows.evidence: Oracle S3 and S4 with Open5GS's UDM, AUSF, PCF, SMF and AMF against our UDR (OUR_UDR=1): the subscriber is provisioned in Open5GS's document format and UERANSIM registers, opens a PDU session, pings and releases it. scripts/g5c_regress.sh --oracle runs S3 and S4 this way.

rows.procedure: Open5GS as the reference: the same requests to its UDR (over MongoDB) and to ours, with the documents of the reference written into ours first; statuses and attribute sets compared, every accepted difference written down with its reason
rows.evidence: 28 requests; the documents of the reference are accepted by our validator except the SSC-mode list that violates the schema.

rows.procedure: 26 schema references into specifications that are not pinned (TS 29.122, 29.514, 29.518, 29.522, 29.544, 29.551, 29.554, 29.572) accept any value: BDT, traffic influence, service parameter and IPTV details are not validated
rows.evidence: Downloading those specifications needs the owner's permission; the generator lists the references.

rows.procedure: PFD change notifications (ApplicationDataChangeNotif.pfdData, TS 29.551) are not sent; monResItems of a policy data subscription is not supported
the implicit subscription of the UDM to permanent subscription data (the UDR selects a UDM through the NRF to notify a provisioning change)
rows.evidence: Subscriptions are explicit; the UDM does not yet subscribe to the data it caches (it caches nothing).

rows.procedure: feature negotiation (supportedFeatures is stored, not negotiated), DELETE of a subscription collection by query filters, 3gpp-Sbi-Message-Priority
the group data aggregates (5g-vn-groups/internal, pp-profile-data, group-identifiers) are stored documents, not derived from the groups
PostgreSQL: one database, no sharding, schema version 1 only, the records gauge counts this process's changes after start; replication and failover are the database's

Nnssf_NSSelection for the registration procedure: allowed NSSAI from the requested and the subscribed S-NSSAIs filtered by the slices that are configured and by the tracking area, rejected in the PLMN and in the TA, configured NSSAI when nothing valid was requested or defaultConfiguredSnssaiInd is set, target AMF set (the requesting AMF's own set when it covers the allowed NSSAI) and candidate AMFs
rows.evidence: Replayed requests of 22 shapes (fuzz seeds); the allowed-NSSAI rules are those of TS 23.501 5.15.5.

rows.procedure: Nnssf_NSSelection for the PDU session establishment: the network slice instance (NSI information: the NRF to use for the slice, nsiId, NRF management and token URIs); 403 SNSSAI_NOT_SUPPORTED for a slice that is not configured; the NRF is named by the API URI of its NFDiscovery service
rows.evidence: Oracle S3 with our NSSF in place of Open5GS's (OUR_NSSF=1): it registers at the NRF and the core completes registration, PDU session and release; Open5GS's AMF asks an NSSF only on the home-routed roaming path, so the answers are compared by the differential. The differential gives the same status and the same NRF as Open5GS's NSSF for five requests (sd FFFFFF, tracking area, local breakout).

rows.procedure: Nnssf_NSSelection for the UE configuration update: configured NSSAI (and allowed NSSAI when requested) for the subscribed S-NSSAIs of the UE
Nnssf_NSSelection for the PDN connection establishment (interworking with EPS): the S-NSSAI the PDN connection maps to, with the roaming mapping of the home PLMN

roaming: requested and subscribed S-NSSAIs of a home PLMN are mapped to the serving PLMN's by the configured mapping; the allowed NSSAI carries mappedHomeSnssai and the answer mappingOfNssai; a slice restricted for a home PLMN is rejected

query handling: nf-type and nf-id are required, exactly one of the four slice information parameters, JSON-encoded parameters, supported-features; a malformed or missing parameter is 400 with the cause and the invalid parameter
rows.evidence: The differential gives 400 for a missing nf-id, nf-type and slice information, as Open5GS's NSSF does.

rows.procedure: Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability update: PUT of the NSSAI supported per tracking area of an AMF (NssaiAvailabilityInfo; 200 with the authorized part, 403 for slices that are not configured or are restricted, 400 for a malformed body); PATCH (JSON Patch) and DELETE (204)

Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability subscribe: POST to /subscriptions with nfNssaiAvailabilityUri, the tracking areas and the expiry chosen by the NSSF (never more than max_lifetime_s), a bound on the number of subscriptions; modify (PATCH of expiry, SUMOD feature) and unsubscribe (DELETE)

Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability notify: NssfEventNotification with the authorized NSSAI per tracking area to the subscribers when an AMF's update changes it, delivered by a worker thread (bounded queue, retries), expired subscriptions removed
rows.evidence: A real callback server receives the notification in the test.

rows.procedure: Nnssf_NSSAIAvailability OPTIONS: 200 with Accept-Encoding: identity (RFC 7694; no content coding is supported)
supported features: the NSSF keeps and answers the intersection of what the consumer offered and what it supports (availability: ONSSAI, SUMOD, EANAN; selection: RSIPCE)
registration at the NRF with the two services (nnssf-nsselection v2, nnssf-nssaiavailability v1); the AMF discovers it without a configured address
rows.evidence: Oracle S3 with our NSSF in place of Open5GS's (OUR_NSSF=1): it registers at the NRF and the core completes registration, PDU session and release; Open5GS's AMF asks an NSSF only on the home-routed roaming path, so the answers are compared by the differential. The cluster tests start the NSSF with the other functions.

rows.procedure: configuration: slices (S-NSSAI, NRF, tracking areas or TAC ranges, restriction per home PLMN), AMF sets, roaming mappings, policy limits, subscriptions, state file; every wrong value is refused at start with the key that is wrong
rows.evidence: 11 bad configurations are rejected by the binary.

rows.procedure: state: subscriptions and the NSSAI availability of the AMFs survive a restart (write-behind state file, atomic replace, a damaged file refused)
hostile input: replay fuzzing of selection and availability requests and notifications (30,000 mutations under ASan in the regression)
every body the NSSF produces (selection answers for the four procedures, ProblemDetails 403 and 400, subscription created, availability info, notification) validates against the OpenAPI of TS 29.531
